methods.label: Use the product of the roots
methods.explanation:
For a quadratic whose leading coefficient is \(1\), the constant term is the product of its two roots. This follows by expanding the root factors:
\[
(x-a)(x-b)=x^2-(a+b)x+ab.
\]
Comparing with \(x^2-mx+2\) gives \(ab=2\). In particular, neither \(a\) nor \(b\) is zero, so the reciprocals in the question are defined.

Applying the same constant-term rule to the second quadratic, we can find \(q\) without finding either root individually:
\[
\begin{aligned}
q&=\left(a+\frac1b\right)\left(b+\frac1a\right)\\
 &=ab+\frac aa+\frac bb+\frac1{ab}\\
 &=2+1+1+\frac12\\
 &=\boxed{\frac92}.
\end{aligned}
\]
The answer is choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
